notes:
HSE INDICATORS - TALKING POINTS (cut-off Oct 26, 2026; Oct figures pending data load)

DAFWCF - Lost-time case frequency. Lost-time cases (DAFWC) x 10^6 / man-hours worked (HHT). Target 0. Aug-Sep: 0.
TRICF - Total recordable case frequency. (FAT + DAFWC + MTC + RWC) x 10^6 / HHT. Target 2.35 (range 2.35-3.00). Aug-Sep: 0.00, within target.
TVCR - Total vehicle accident rate. Work-related vehicle accidents x 10^6 / km travelled. Target 0.79 (range 0.79-2.00). Aug-Sep: 0.00, within target.
FAC - First aid cases. Reported for visibility, no target. Aug-Sep: 0.
HHT - Man-hours worked (denominator of TRICF/DAFWCF). Km driven - denominator of TVCR. Total workers - headcount in the month.

How to read the charts: bars = number of cases (left axis); green line = frequency (right axis); red dashed line = target (right axis). Frequency below the dashed line means the indicator is within target.
Pyramid (cumulative since Aug-26): FAT / DAFWC (top), MTC / RWC, FAC, incidents, and safety observations at the base. A wide base with an empty top is the expected profile: many proactive observations, no injuries.
Pending for Oct-26: all values marked in red must be loaded in the Compressor Plant and Pipeline monthly workbooks before issuing.

Background: 
Vaca Muerta upstream major companies (including PAE, YPF & Pampa) have a contract with MODENA for the provision of its services which consists of having a helicopter available for use in the event of a medical emergency.
Vista holds and manages a contract with MODENA covering aeromedical evacuation services for operators in Neuquén.
VMOS has a contract in force with MODENA for such services. The service originated as an ad hoc decision by YPF following an Emergency Response Risk Analysis. 

Geographic Dispersion
SMP pipeline route extends over 473 km along 2 provinces with sections located far away from high-complexity medical centres  Ground transportation may compromise the critical response time window during an emergency.

Labour Context
Impact of the VMOS precedent in the event of an accident requiring this service 
UOCRA agreement does not “explicitly” require this service for VMOS or SMP.

Actual Use, No Saturation
Existing regional contracts (Neuquén and VMOS) recorded 40 to 50 emergencies over 3 years (approximately 1 to 2 per month), indicating there is operational capacity to include the SMP route.

Proposal to be discussed with Shareholders:
Given the project’s extensive geographical footprint which includes remote areas with limited or no access to adequate medical infrastructure, it is recommended to have a helicopter available for emergency medical evacuation, particularly for incidents requiring medium- or high-complexity medical care.
